name: Surrender and wrecks
description: Gameplay change (off by default; Other Empires page, Gameplay changes). A badly crippled AI ship (less than 45% of its components working, and no way to run: engines out, or slower than what is shooting at it and unable to jump away) that is outgunned (the ships shooting at it have 1.5 times its own firepower) may strike its colours instead of fighting to the death. The chance each check depends on its people's temper (cautious races give in sooner, aggressive ones fight on). A ship that has struck stops fighting and moving, leaves its fleet and is no longer fired at; the nearest armed enemy puts a prize crew aboard within 20 seconds (reusing the original's boarding capture: the empire's capture policy decides whether the ship is kept, retrofitted or scrapped). Nobody comes: after 120 game days its crew takes it back. Ships that are destroyed leave wrecks (the Wreckage and Salvage add-on's debris fields, with its own settings and map markers): construction and mining ships salvage them for resources and sometimes a technology the wreck's builders had; wrecks decay (3 years by default) and each system holds at most 12, the oldest crumbling first, so long wars do not pile up objects. AI construction ships salvage when no armed enemy is near. Your own ships never surrender on their own.
